sentences.text: Scientists estimated this bird's body mass at roughly 2 kilograms, a weight comparable to modern Bar-headed and Egyptian geese.
The single known species, A. tortonica, is known only from fossil bones of a left leg found in the Hammerschmiede clay pits near Pforzen.
Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme named the genus in 2022, combining the local region name with the Greek word for goose.
This extinct bird belongs to the family Anatidae.
Fossils of this genus date to the Tortonian stage of the Miocene epoch, living between 11.63 and 7.246 million years ago.
It inhabited the Hammerschmiede clay pits in Bavaria, Germany.
